title: Saute de Veau Marengo
subtitle: A Provencal veal stew with tomato, white wine, and mushrooms
excerpt: Browned veal shoulder braised in tomato, white wine, and stock with mushrooms and a gremolata finish. A stew with Provencal roots and a clean, bright flavour.
sourceNotes: Classic French braised veal dish. The gremolata of lemon, parsley, and garlic stirred in at the end is traditional and lifts the whole pot.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the gremolata. Thaw overnight, reheat gently, and add fresh gremolata before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a large casserole and add 20 minutes to the braise time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew improves overnight. Reheat gently and add gremolata just before serving.

content.text: Veal shoulder becomes tender and light after a long, gentle braise. Brown the meat in batches so it sears rather than steams. The gremolata stirred in at the end is the finishing touch that keeps the dish from feeling heavy.
Pat the veal dry and season with salt and pepper. Dust lightly with flour and shake off the excess.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in the dutch oven over high heat. Brown the veal in two batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil and the onion. Cook for 6 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and tomato puree. Stir for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 3 minutes.
Return the veal to the pot. Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, and thyme. The liquid should just cover the meat.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 60 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook uncovered for a further 20 minutes to reduce the sauce slightly.
Mix the lemon zest, parsley, and grated garlic together. Remove the bay and thyme from the stew. Stir in the gremolata and serve.

items.symptom: The veal is tough after an hour.
items.cause: The heat was too high or the pieces were too large.
items.fix: Keep the simmer very gentle. Add 20 to 30 minutes and check again. Shoulder needs long, slow cooking.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: The mushrooms released a lot of liquid, or the braise was covered throughout.
items.fix: Cook uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes at the end to reduce the sauce.

items.symptom: The flavour tastes sharp or tomato-heavy.
items.cause: The wine or tomatoes need balancing.
items.fix: Add a pinch of sugar and a small knob of butter. Stir and taste again.
